literal: Even if they come piled up, the distress encountered by him who has no despair will itself suffer distress.
translation: Even if troubles come crowding in waves, the distress met by a person who does not despair will itself suffer distress and flee.
modern: துன்பங்கள் அடுக்கடுக்காக வந்தாலும், மனத்தளர்ச்சி இல்லாதவன் அடையும் துன்பமானது தானே துன்பப்பட்டு அழிந்துவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet uses a powerful personification of distress to show the strength of resilience. The poet states that when a person of undaunted spirit, who refuses to sink into despair (அழிவிலான்), encounters difficulties, those difficulties cannot break him. Even if troubles pile up one after another (அடுக்கி வரினும்), the distress itself gets distressed (இடுக்கண் இடுக்கட்படும்) and is defeated by his unwavering courage. Ultimately, resilience turns the tables on adversity, making the trouble itself suffer failure.
